scope: Focused text-only editorial review of immutable source segments 801–880 (80 segments). All 358 source word occurrences are preserved in exact order and spelling: 326 eligible, 31 explicitly excluded nonspoken sound/action-description occurrences, and one unresolved spelling hold at 839:w06 Nikah (standard dictionary nikâh), without changing the source. Every eligible occurrence has a contextual Arabic explanation and a four-option choice override; 12 clips have no eligible occurrences and are wholly non-educational. Personal names remain eligible even inside action descriptions: Memo at 865:w01 is explicitly described as a written name, not claimed to be audible. Speaker-role labels accompanying intelligible dialogue, meaningful interjections, colloquial forms, intelligible sung words and the truncated obscene utterance sik are retained. Ayşem is retained as a documented connected personal-name/affectionate formation, without claiming the character's official name or certifying standard possessive punctuation. The primary MEB witness supports hiçbirini in the sung question, not certification of all film lyrics: source dünyaya, kul and geldik are not replaced with other published lyric variants. Context distinguishes bir tek atayım as drinking one glass, sahip çıkacak as care, dalyan gibi as tall and well-built, bok anladın as sarcastic negation, and gördü at 834 as third-person past, not second-person despite the source Arabic translation. The blue-eye interpretation of mavi mavi is explicitly contextual; no eye colour is independently verified. Insults are explained descriptively without endorsement, and the cut-off verb is not silently completed. References are linguistic evidence metadata only. No audiovisual verification, native-speaker certification, device acceptance, or full-film editorial acceptance is claimed.
